title: Moving from Net 30 also lists a customer stored as "NET 30"
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: Your shop has a customer on Net 30 and an older one stored as "NET 30" in capitals.
  • You are an Admin user working at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • COD is the shop's default for new customers.
  • Customer {Customer-A} holds Net 30 and customer {Customer-B} is stored with the text "NET 30" (from an old import).
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S4-03 Alpha and {Customer-B} is ZZAUTOTEST S4-03 Upper.
  • Starting screen: the Credit Terms page (Settings, then "Credit Terms" in the Finance group), Active tab.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click the "⋯" at the right of the "Net 30" row.
  2. Click "Move Customers".
  3. Type the start their names share in "Search customers".
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the menu opens.
  • Step 2: a window titled "Move Customers from Net 30" opens.
  • Step 3: the list shows both {Customer-A} and {Customer-B}, each ticked.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11673 (Story 4, Move Customers)

  • S4-R3: “The list holds every customer whose term matches this term ignoring capitals and spaces. On COD it also holds customers with a blank term. The Counter Sale customer is never listed.”
  • Assumptions: “Stored customer and vendor terms carry inconsistent spellings from old imports and migrations (for example "NET 30" and "Due On Receipt"); every count, match and move treats names as equal when they differ only in capitals and spaces.”
